answers.M8-S1: The author did an experiment to see if his Mason-bees could find their way home after being carried far away, and some of them did.
answers.M8-S2: To show the weather got windy, which made it harder for the bees to fly home because they had to stay low.
answers.M8-S3: It suggests they stopped at flowers on the way and collected food, so the trip was not too hard for them.
answers.M8-S4: So he could tell his bees apart from other bees when they got back to the nest.
answers.M8-S5: On the way home he was hardly thinking about the bees at all, but then he got excited when Aglaé told him two had come back.
answers.M8-S6: It goes in time order, telling the steps of the experiment from catching the bees to them coming home.
answers.M8-S7: To show how fast the bees flew home, even though they also stopped to get pollen.
answers.M8-S8: To show that marking the bees was hard and he hurt some, so only about twenty could really fly home.
answers.M8-S9: The wind kept them low, so they did not get to see the countryside on the trip, they just flew along the ground.
